research_question: If a downstream provider durably accepts an effect inside the exact V15/V16 guarded provider-commit window but the Frank process hard-exits before the provider call returns and before local outcome recording, does current v6+V14 state preserve uncertainty and later reconcile/re-enter without resurrecting the dead execution capability?
hypothesis: Provider acceptance followed by caller ack-loss/process death leaves the durable Frank effect at COMMITTING with no fabricated outcome; persistent execution-binding bytes remain provenance only; independent outcome evidence may reconcile and re-enter without reviving effect authority.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Hard process death inside the provider commit critical section either corrupts/strands the lifecycle so it cannot reconcile cleanly, or causes downstream acceptance to be promoted to local success without independent evidence.

selected_opportunity.reason: Fresh target-v6 evidence had already closed the exact-generation B1/B2/B3 mechanism discriminator; the highest-value remaining bounded uncertainty was timeout/ack-loss after provider acceptance and before local outcome recording.

exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.name: GO_OOB_PROVIDER_ACK_LOSS_CRASH_RECONCILIATION
exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.causal_intervention: Real Gate + admitted V16 + caller-bound fence -> B1 reserve -> B2 COMMITTING -> guarded B3 -> separate FULL-synchronous SQLite provider ledger commit/fsync -> os._exit(73) before local outcome recording -> independent observation/reconciliation -> provenance re-entry.

target_environment.kernel: Linux 6.8.0-117-generic #117-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue May 5 19:26:24 UTC 2026 x86_64

external_primary_evidence.source: Stripe official error handling / idempotency documentation
external_primary_evidence.supports: Connection/API failure may leave result indeterminate; same idempotency key can make retries safe where provider semantics support it; independent outcome observation/webhooks are used for reconciliation.
After intermittent failure the client may not know whether the server received the request; retry with the same key is provider-specific and server-error outcomes can remain indeterminate.
A client may be uncertain whether an operation completed after timeout or network disruption; durable revision/ownership primitives do not eliminate outcome uncertainty at a remote boundary.
Revisions and lock ownership keys provide compareable/fenceable ownership identity and atomic transaction guards.

supported: The current v6 exact-generation fence and V14 lifecycle can represent the provider-accepted/caller-died gap without fabricating a local success/failure.
Persistent execution-generation binding is provenance only; it cannot reconstruct the transient execution capability after process death.
Outcome observation/reconciliation is correctly separable from effect authority and can survive generation death.
Provenance-bound re-entry can close the reconciled lifecycle to COMPLETE after independently observed success.
not_supported_or_not_claimed: No claim that arbitrary providers are exactly-once.
No claim that every real provider supports idempotency keys or outcome lookup/webhooks.
No closure of the real-provider timeout-after-acceptance acceptance gate.
No promotion of PR 250/255 into main from this receipt.
analysis.counterhypothesis_outcome: REFUTED_FOR_THIS_SYNTHETIC_MECHANISM: the hard exit did not corrupt or prematurely resolve the lifecycle; the strongest remaining counterhypothesis moves to real provider semantics and production routing/lowering rather than the local uncertainty/reconciliation state machine.

architecture_delta.decision: Preserve the v6 design split: transient exact execution capability gates start/retry/provider commit; durable effect state records uncertainty; reconciliation accepts evidence after generation turnover without granting effect authority.
architecture_delta.promotion_impact: Strengthens F-V01-09/F-V01-13 evidence but does not itself close real-provider or production-routing gates.

test_obligations: Run an actual configured provider connector/test-mode equivalent that can produce acceptance followed by lost/indeterminate acknowledgement, with same-key replay semantics verified from that provider's contract.
Prove ordinary production effect routing/lowering cannot bypass CallerBoundEffectLifecycleRuntime + guarded_provider_commit.
Carry exact ClayCode frontend/TypedIR/compiler/lowering receipts for the production effect path, not semantic-source markers alone.
Exercise recovery generation/rollback with provider-uncertain effects and verify outcome observation survives while effect authority does not.
negative_results_preserved: The experiment does not demonstrate a need for a new two-phase commit protocol across arbitrary providers.
The experiment does not justify reviving stale execution authority for retry; reconciliation succeeded without it.
next_frontier: F-V01-13 recovery generation/rollback around uncertain external effects
